THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners in both these petitions have sought for a writ in the nature of mandamus to direct respondent Nos.1 to 5 not to utilize their lands without initiating proceedings to acquire it under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation, Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation, Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: They have also sought for a direction to respondent Nos.1 to 5 to consider NC: 2024:KHC-K:4984 their representations before widening the road between Dhangapur to Nimbarga via Battarga village, Aland Taluka and Kalaburagi District.
They also sought for a writ in the nature of mandamus to initiate acquisition proceedings also for the lands utilized in the year 1996 and pay compensation.

2. The petitioners contend that they are the owners of lands in various survey numbers of Nimbarga,
Battarga and Basavantwadi villages.

The petitioners contend that a 10' cart road runs from Dhangapur to Nimbarga via Battarga village passing over their lands and some of the petitioners contend that a road measuring 15' was formed by the respondents to reach Nimbarga Tanda without initiating acquisition proceedings.
The petitioners contend that the respondents are now intending to widen it into by 100' without following due process of law.

The petitioners contend that they had submitted representations requesting respondent Nos.1 to 5 not to dispossess them without following the due process of law NC: 2024:KHC-K:4984 and alleged that the respondents have not considered their representations but are trying to dispossess them from their properties for the proposed widening.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners reiterated and submitted that right to property is a constitutional right and the petitioners cannot be dispossessed without following the due process of law.
He submits that the due process of law is nothing but issuing appropriate notification notifying the properties of the petitioners and paying compensation along with all statutory benefits.

He submits that the respondents are duty bound to comply with the above, failing which, the action on the part of the respondents should be treated as unconstitutional and deserves to be interfered with.
submit that the respondents are trying to widen and develop the existing road and that the same does not involve acquisition of any lands belonging to the petitioners.

5 petitioners had NC: 2024:KHC-K:4984 submitted representations, the same shall be considered in accordance with law.

sentences.text: In both these petitions, the petitioners claimed to be the owners of several parcels of lands in Nimbarga, Battarga and Basavantwad villages, Aland Taluka and Kalaburagi District.
They all contend that the respondents are trying to widen an existing road to a 100' road by utilizing their properties and without following the due process of law.
The petitioners alleged that the respondents are trying to take over their properties without passing appropriate awards and without paying compensation.

If the lands of the petitioners are required by the respondents for whatever purpose, the respondents are bound to comply with the due process of law by issuing appropriate notification and determining the compensation payable.
The respondents cannot use the properties belonging to the petitioners under the garb of widening the road.

This is also the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kolkata Municipal NC: 2024:KHC-K:4984 Corporation and Another vs. Bimal Kumar Shah and Others reported in 2024 SCC Online SC 968.

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondents are liable to be directed to consider the representations of the petitioners and proceed in accordance with law.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Both these writ petitions are allowed in part.
(ii) The respondents are directed to consider the representations of the petitioners and dispose them off in accordance with law.

(iii) In order to enable the respondents toe consider the representations of the petitioners.
(iv) The petitioners are directed to furnish a copy of their representation to respondent No.2, 3 and 4 who shall consider them and pass appropriate orders within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of representations.
